claims.text: Temperature-pulsed annealing preserves the metastable solid-solution state of multi-element nanoparticles better than conventional isothermal annealing.
Limited atomic diffusion during temperature pulses kinetically suppresses complete phase separation.
Limited atomic diffusion during temperature pulses kinetically suppresses nanoparticle sintering.
The target materials are multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles with low noble-metal content produced by physical or chemical methods.
The proposed treatment consists of annealing at 773 K followed by three to five 5-minute pulses at 1173 K with controlled cooling between pulses.
An inert atmosphere minimizes oxidation during the treatment.
The 773–1173 K treatment window is relevant to catalytic service and overlaps the stated thermoelectric service range.
Pulsed heating activates atomic diffusion sufficient for local rearrangement without permitting full phase separation.
Transient diffusion permits local atomic shuffling that relieves internal stresses.
Transient diffusion reduces minor compositional fluctuations.
Rapid cooling prevents diffusion from progressing to full phase separation.
Rapid cooling prevents diffusion from progressing to sintering.
Prolonged isothermal annealing allows atoms to reach thermodynamically favored segregated states.
Pulsed-annealed nanoparticles will retain greater elemental and phase homogeneity than continuously annealed nanoparticles.
Pulsed-annealed nanoparticles will exhibit less phase segregation than continuously annealed nanoparticles.
Pulsed-annealed nanoparticles will exhibit less sintering than continuously annealed nanoparticles.
The mechanism applies when atomic mobility is appreciable but insufficient to produce complete equilibration during each pulsed treatment.
The mechanism may not apply at much higher noble-metal contents.
The mechanism may not apply to substantially different nanoparticle sizes where surface effects dominate.
Surface oxidation or other side reactions could alter the observed structural outcomes.
